title: Bernardinus of Siena: Mary did more for God than God for man—Rivet and Drelincourt collect the sayings
source_text: LXXIII. Neque haec adhuc videntur ipsis satis. Addunt Virginem plus fecisse Deo, quam videtur ipse Deus fecisse generi humano. Postquam enim Bernardinus alter, nempe Senensis, qui fuit in numerum Sanctorum relatus, longam comparationem inter Deum & Beatam Virginem instituit, concludit tandem his verbis, Reddendo ergo singula singulis scilicet quod fecit Deus homini, & quod fecit Beata Virgo ipsi Deo, videtis, ut pro solatio dicere liceat, quod plus Maria Deo, quam ipse Deus homini fecit: Unde Deus propter Virginem obligatur nobis plurimum. Quae pluribus deducta, & suis locis citata videre est, apud Andream Rivetum, lib. 2. Apologiae pro Sanctissima Virgine Maria. Et apud Carolum Drelincourtium libris accurate & prolixe scriptis de Honore Beatae Virgini Mariae debito: ex quibus haec modo de multis excerpta sunt: & ad quos curiosum lectorem remittimus, si cui plura hujusmodi legere, & apud authores inquirere libeat.
pass_a_gloss: Nor do these things yet seem enough to them. They add that the Virgin did more for God than God Himself seems to have done for the human race. For after another Bernardinus, namely of Siena, who was enrolled in the number of the Saints, instituted a long comparison between God and the Blessed Virgin, he concludes at last with these words: Rendering therefore each to each, namely what God did for man and what the Blessed Virgin did for God Himself, you see that for consolation it may be said that Mary did more for God than God Himself did for man: Whence God is bound to us very much on account of the Virgin. Which things, drawn out more fully and cited in their places, may be seen in Andrew Rivet, book 2 of the Apology for the most Holy Virgin Mary. And in Charles Drelincourt in books accurately and at length written on the Honor due to the Blessed Virgin Mary: from which these things have now been excerpted from many: and to whom we send back the curious reader, if anyone please to read more of this kind and to inquire among the authors.
pass_b_english: Bernardinus of Siena: Mary did more for God than God for humankind—so God is much obliged to us for her sake.
Rivet and Drelincourt gather such sayings; Le Blanc sends the curious reader there.
